Priya: Quick clarification from the Q&A: when we say our mission is to make inference predictable and economical, what's the single most important metric leadership wants product and marketing to push?

Elena (CEO): Focus on three measurable things. Primary: p99 latency vs SLO (ms). Secondary: $/1M tokens (billing metric). Tertiary: percent of requests that hit cache or cheaper variant (efficiency). Use these in decks.

Marco (Head of Strategy): From a market POV, that lets us segment messaging: developer-first startups care about speed to launch and price; platform teams care about observability and rollouts; enterprise cares about SLAs and private options.

Omar (Sales): Could we get a one-liner for pitch decks that isn't generic? Something like "predictable inference across hosted, dedicated, and private" felt close but a bit dry.

Zoe (Marketing): How about: "Turn model capability into predictable product outcomes: stable latency, transparent costs, and enterprise controls." Short, outcome-focused.

Nikhil (Eng): Technical note for claims: when we cite p99 numbers, let's also include the workload shape (short chat vs long context). Benchmarks without context lead to objections.

Elena (CEO): Exactly. Always attach the workload profile. And for competitor comparisons, prefer archetypes not name-dropping: "Cloud provider: model breadth, infra lock-in risk"; "Model API: easy access, variable economics"; "Self-host: ops tax, tuning burden." Those three cover the objection landscape.

Omar (Sales): Customers often say "we can self-host for cheaper." Quick rebuttal?

Marco (Head of Strategy): Rebuttal: self-hosting hides ops cost and tuning complexity. Our value: predictable unit economics + operational guardrails out of the box. Example: a customer reduced effective token cost by ~40% after enabling cache + batching; we can include that as a case study.

Priya (PM): Actionable ask: Sales wants a one-pager + two-slide tech appendix (benchmarks + brief config guidance) by next Wed. Can engineering and research commit?

Nikhil (Eng): Yes. We'll produce: 1) benchmark results for short-chat and long-context by Tue, 2) recommended config mappings (dynamic batching, 8-bit quant, KV cache tips) as a bullet list.

Zoe (Marketing): I'll draft three short headlines and a micro-site blurb for review. Want to avoid "best models" language and keep numbers up front.

Elena (CEO): Good. Also: product roadmap note 1: prioritize observability (per-route cost + latency breakdown) and rollout controls for next two sprints. Private/on-prem packaging remains important but can be staged after these hosted wins.

Omar (Sales): Any guidance for AEs about rebuttals to CloudVendor who claims "we have global infra + SLAs"?

Marco (Head of Strategy): Response: they have scale, but often with mixed economics and vendor lock-in. We compete on being deployment-flexible (hosted to private), offering transparent unit costs, and a runtime optimized for inference economics.

Priya (PM): Can we capture this thread into a short FAQ for internal enablement? I can draft and circulate by Fri.

Elena (CEO): Action items: 1) @Nikhil deliver benchmarks Tue. 2) @Marco & @Priya produce sales one-pager + FAQ by Wed. 3) @Zoe draft marketing copy by Thu. I'll review mid-Thu. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

all-hands-bot: Thread closed. Recording and slides will be posted to #all-hands-resources.
